beats.intro: Chapter fifty-three. [[sub]]When four terms share no common factor, try factoring them in pairs.
beats.idea: Take a x plus a y plus b x plus b y. [[none]]No factor is shared by all four terms. [[group]]So group them in pairs: the first two, and the last two. [[f1]]Factor a out of the first pair: a times x plus y. [[f2]]Factor b out of the second: b times x plus y. [[same]]Now both parts share the same factor, x plus y. [[pull]]Pull it out, just like a GCF: [[ans]]x plus y, times a plus b.
beats.area: An area model shows why. [[tiles]]Arrange the four terms as the parts of one rectangle: [[rows]]a x and a y share the height a, [[rows2]]and b x and b y share the height b. [[cols]]The columns share the widths x and y. [[sides]]So the whole rectangle is a plus b tall and x plus y wide: [[ans]]its area is the product of those two factors.
beats.ex: Try p q minus three q plus four p minus twelve. [[group]]Group the first two terms and the last two. [[f1]]The first pair has a common q: q times p minus three. [[f2]]The second pair has a common four: four times p minus three. [[same]]Both share p minus three, [[ans]]so the factored form is p minus three, times q plus four. [[chk]]Multiply back to check: you get all four terms again.
beats.neg: Watch the signs when the third term is negative. [[q]]Factor m x minus m y minus n x plus n y. [[f1]]The first pair gives m times x minus y. [[f2]]For the second pair, factor out negative n, [[flip]]and the signs inside both flip: negative n times x minus y. [[same]]Now both parts share x minus y, [[ans]]so the answer is x minus y, times m minus n. [[warn]]If the parentheses don't match, check the signs before giving up.
beats.gcf: Always look for a GCF of all the terms first. [[q]]Here, every term has m squared n squared. [[out]]Factor it out first. [[left]]Inside, twelve m cubed minus eight m squared plus nine m n cubed minus six n cubed. [[pairs]]Now group: four m squared times three m minus two, plus three n cubed times three m minus two. [[ans]]The result is m squared n squared, times three m minus two, times four m squared plus three n cubed.
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[w1]]Factor out any GCF of all the terms first. [[w2]]Group the four terms in pairs, and factor each pair. [[w3]]If the two parts share a binomial, factor it out. [[w4]]Watch the signs when you factor out a negative. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
beats.final3: Last one. Factor out the GCF first.
beats.finish: Nice work. That's the end of chapter fifty-three, factoring by grouping.
